abstentions: Cannot establish a complete or universally applicable account of how Child DLA interacts with PIP.
Cannot determine whether a particular child will be invited to claim PIP, when DLA will end, whether payments will continue without interruption, or whether PIP will be awarded.
Cannot establish current law or an individual entitlement or payment outcome.
Cannot calculate any award or infer missing conditions from the selected material.

evidence.quote:
P1001 [See ADM memo 11-25] PIP was introduced for new claimants from 8.4.131 in certain areas only
(see ADM Chapter P5 Appendix 1 for the postcodes affected). It was introduced in all other areas for new

claimants only from 10.6.132. For existing DLA claimants PIP was introduced after 27.10.13, but only
where a relevant date has been specified. It replaces DLA for working age claimants. PIP is an extra
costs benefit for people who have a limited or severely limited ability to carry out daily living or mobility
activities.


Note: See ADM Chapter P5 for the definition of relevant date and for guidance on transitional provisions.

P1003 Those claimants already entitled to DLA on 8.4.13 will continue to retain that benefit until a
decision is made on their entitlement to PIP at a later date (see ADM Chapter P5).

claims.scope_or_qualification: This is frozen, machine-extracted ADM guidance, not current-law assurance. The first passage limits the transition statement to existing DLA claimants for whom a relevant date has been specified; the second concerns claimants already entitled to DLA on 8 April 2013. The package does not establish complete continuity rules or applicability to a particular child, date or territory.
claims.statement: Within the captured ADM guidance, PIP replaces DLA for working-age claimants, while people already entitled to DLA on 8 April 2013 retain it until a later PIP entitlement decision.

evidence.quote:
P5018 The Secretary of State will send an invitation to claim PIP to a DLA entitled person who reaches

the age of 16 after 27.10.13, or as soon as reasonably practicable after the person reaches that age 1.


                                                                                     1 PIP (TP) Reg, reg 3(3)


P5019 However, P5018 will only apply where


1. the Secretary of State has specified a relevant date which applies to the DLA entitled person and


2. the DLA entitled person reaches age 16 on or after the relevant date 1.


                                                                                  1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(3A)


P5020 P5018 does not apply where, on the day they reach the age of 16, the person is entitled to DLA

on the basis of being terminally ill1 within the meaning of ADM P2077.

claims.scope_or_qualification: This does not establish a universal automatic transfer at age 16. It is conditional on DLA entitlement, the relevant date and the stated temporal cohort, and includes the terminal-illness exception. Other exceptions and territorial rules may apply.
claims.statement: The captured transition guidance says that an invitation is sent when a DLA-entitled person reaches age 16 after 27 October 2013, but only where the Secretary of State has specified an applicable relevant date and the person reaches 16 on or after that date; a terminal-illness exception is stated.

evidence.quote:
Claimants under 16

P5025 No claim may be made by a claimant who has not reached age 16, regardless of whether they are

or are not entitled to DLA1.


                                                                                     1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 5

claims.scope_or_qualification: This is a claim rule in the captured transitional guidance, not a complete statement of Child DLA entitlement, payment or continuity. Territorial and current legal applicability remain unresolved.
claims.statement: Under the captured transitional guidance, a person under 16 cannot claim PIP, whether or not they are entitled to DLA.

evidence.quote:
Age

P1013 To be entitled to PIP for the first time a claimant must be

1. age 16 or over and


2. the relevant age of


      2.1 under age 651 or


      2.2 under pensionable age, whichever is the higher and


3. not in receipt of DLA.


Note 1: See DMG 74022 and Appendix 1-4 of DMG Chapter 74 for changes to the pensionable age as
that gradually increases.


Note 2: See ADM Chapter P4 for guidance on exceptions to entitlement for upper age condition.

claims.scope_or_qualification: The heading and continuation span separate selected pages. This concerns first-time PIP entitlement and expressly points to exceptions for the upper-age condition; it must not be treated as the complete transition rule for an existing Child DLA award.
claims.statement: The captured general PIP age guidance says first-time PIP entitlement requires the claimant to be at least 16, below the specified upper relevant age, and not receiving DLA.

gaps: The package expressly marks both applicable requirements as insufficient and lacks complete transition/invitation, age, claim and continuity rules from the appropriate PIP/ADM and territorial sources.
Applicability, benefit regime, relevant date, territory, legal version, amendment history and independent specialist review remain unresolved.
The resolved concept “Benefit interaction” has no applicable evidence requirement, so its evidence completeness cannot be established.

The package is truncated: only the highest-ranked pages fitted the lexical candidate limit, and a whole item concerning regulation 44 of the Social Security (General Benefit) Regulations 1982 was omitted for the byte budget.
Conditions on adjacent pages and unmodelled cross-references may be absent. In particular, cited definitions, appendices and exceptions are not supplied completely.

The cross-border material concerns moves from England and Wales to Scotland and dated devolved-benefit changes; it does not complete the general Child DLA-to-PIP transition question or establish Northern Ireland rules.
limitations: Independent experimental staff-question research; independent human and specialist review remains pending.
Selected guidance consists of frozen machine extractions whose applicability is unreviewed; capture dates are not publication, commencement or applicability dates.
Project-authored concepts and relationships are proposals, not official guidance or legal implications.
Complete selected units do not constitute a complete statute, consolidated amendment history, dependency closure or legal answer.
The requested source version, territorial extent, commencement and applicability are distinct; some extent information remains unknown.
summary: The frozen package provides partial guidance: PIP replaced DLA for working-age claimants under the described transitional arrangements; existing DLA claimants generally retained DLA until a PIP entitlement decision; and specified age, invitation and claim conditions govern movement from DLA to PIP. However, the package is truncated and expressly lacks complete transition, invitation, age, claim, continuity, territorial and applicability evidence, so it cannot establish the interaction comprehensively or determine an individual outcome.
